Translingual

Symbol

  1. (international standards) ISO 639-3 language code for Pima Bajo.

English

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

pia

  1. (anatomy) The pia mater, the innermost of the meninges that protect the brain and spinal cord.
    • 2009 January 25, Denis Campbell, “Kian, 4, needs a miracle. He's in the right place”, in The Observer‎[1]:
      One screen in the theatre relays live colour pictures of Harkness and his colleague Tiernan Byrnes's progress, cutting and pushing through first the dura, then the arachnoid and finally the pia, the thin, spider's web-type membranes that cover the brain itself.
Derived terms
[edit]
  • pial

Etymology 2

[edit]

Borrowed from Hawaiian pia.

Noun

[edit]

pia (uncountable)

  1. Polynesian arrowroot (Tacca leontopetaloides), whose fleshy tubers yield arrowroot starch.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • api-, IPA, API, IAP, AIP, Api

Esperanto

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *pewH-
Proto-Italic *pwījosder.
Latin pius
Italian pioder.
▲
Latin pius
Old French piu
Middle French pieux
French pieuxder.
▲
Latin piusbor.
English piousder.
Esperanto pia

    From Italian pio, French pieux, English pious, all from Latin pius (“pious, devout”). Compare Spanish pío, Romanian pios.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈpia/
    • Audio:(file)
    • Rhymes: -ia
    • Syllabification: pi‧a

    Adjective

    [edit]

    pia (accusative singular pian, plural piaj, accusative plural piajn)

    1. pious
      Antonym: malpia

    Related terms

    [edit]
    • pieco

    • “pia”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-2026

    Hawaiian

    [edit]

    Etymology 1

    [edit]

    From Proto-Polynesian *pia (compare with Tahitian pia and Samoan pia),[1][2] from Proto-Oceanic *ʀabia “sago, Metroxylon sagu” (compare with Fijian via “Cyrtosperma merkusii (syn. Cyrtosperma chamissonis), Alocasia macrorrhizos (syn. Alocasia indica)”) from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *ʀambia “sago palm” (compare with Malay rumbia).[2][3]

    Noun

    [edit]

    pia

    1. Polynesian arrowroot (Tacca leontopetaloides)
    2. starch from any plant in general (corn etc.)
    3. a variety of taro
    4. a variety of sweet potato

    References

    [edit]
    1. ^ Pukui, Mary Kawena; Elbert, Samuel H. (1986), “pia”, in Hawaiian Dictionary, revised & enlarged edition, Honolulu, HI: University of Hawai'i Press, →ISBN, page 325
    2. ↑ 2.0 2.1 Ross Clark and Simon J. Greenhill, editors (2011), “pia1”, in “POLLEX-Online: The Polynesian Lexicon Project Online”, in Oceanic Linguistics, volume 50, number 2, pages 551-559
    3. ^ Ross, Malcolm D.; Pawley, Andrew; Osmond, Meredith (2016), The lexicon of Proto-Oceanic, volume 5: Plants, Canberra: Australian National University, →ISBN, pages 286-289

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

    From English beer.

    Noun

    [edit]

    pia

    1. beer

    Etymology 3

    [edit]

    (This etymology is missing or incomplete. Please add to it, or discuss it at the Etymology scriptorium.)

    Makasar

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]

    Inherited from Proto-South Sulawesi *pia (“good”), from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *pia (“goodness”).

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈpia/, [ˈpʰi.a]
    • Hyphenation: pi‧a

    Verb

    [edit]

    pia (Lontara spelling ᨄᨗᨕ)

    1. healed, cured (of wound); recovered
      Piami lokoʼna ― His wound has healed
    2. calmed down (of anger)
      Piami larrona ― He has calmed down after being angry
    3. well finished (of war)
      Piami bunduka ― The war has ended well

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    affixations
    • piài

    Further reading

    [edit]
    • Cense, A. A. (1979), Makassaars-Nederlands woordenboek, 's-Gravenhage: Martinus Nijhoff, →ISBN

    Portuguese

    [edit]

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
     
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpi.ɐ/
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpi.ɐ/
      • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpi.a/
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈpi.ɐ/

    • Rhymes: -iɐ
    • Hyphenation: pi‧a

    Etymology 1

    [edit]

    From Old Galician-Portuguese pia, from Latin pīla (“mortar”).[1][2]

    Noun

    [edit]

    pia f (plural pias)

    1. sink (basin with a drain)
    2. a sink and adjacent counter
      Deixe o prato na pia, mas não dentro.
      Leave the plate on the counter, not in the sink.
    3. a basin for holding water, in particular one that is furniture or part of the building rather than a movable object
      pia batismal ― baptismal font
    Descendants

    • → Hunsrik: Bia
